## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics

**2026-04-25 — Personal agentic operating system**  
Source: [AI Daily Brief — “How To Build a Personal Agentic Operating System”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ntvkDnk_5jA)

Summary: The episode lays out a model-neutral workflow for getting better results from agentic tools by maintaining a durable operating layer underneath them: human-readable files for preferences, working context, project state, decision rules, and repeatable workflows. Tools discussed include Codex, Claude Code-style tools, Cursor, Windsurf, and other agentic work environments.

Setup:
1. Create a small text-file knowledge base for how you work, active projects, recurring constraints, and output preferences.
2. Add persistent tool instructions or config files that point the agent at those files.
3. Define reusable workflows for strategy, research, communication, operations, and decision support.
4. After each serious run, update the files with corrections, preferences, and lessons learned.
5. Keep the system tool-neutral so it can move across agent platforms.

Available now: Yes. The method depends on plain text files and existing agent tools.

Why it matters: The practical leverage is not a new model; it is reducing repeated context setup and making agents inherit stable operating assumptions across sessions.

## 8. Notable Voices

**2026-04-26 — Pablo: conversational UI is not the end state**  
Sources: [post 1](https://primal.net/e/881de616477cec9c35e4cfc5dc911a1a36ede998878f89788eeadf393404c5cd), [post 2](https://primal.net/e/cc1f6dd0138e68d00dc0207305e7ddf580bea999204095245087c48d1bcfe5a4), [post 3](https://primal.net/e/2f45006131e967ba86ff095eff2f5219fa1b725a7e33170173262170ff7e2148)

Summary: Pablo argued that voice is likely a strong input mode, but text or voice output should become rarer as agents move from conversation toward action execution.

Why it matters: Useful framing for AI product design: the high-value interface may be less “chat with model” and more “state intent, then inspect completed action.”
